
A task carries direct links to the design rules that govern it (WL-REQ-1356), stored in `task_governed_by (task_id, rule_id, rule_version, source)`. Accepting a plan links every task it publishes to each rule the plan's `covers` edges point at. Each `covers` edge runs from the plan to one rule, resolved from the plan's `covers` entries when the plan was written (WL-REQ-1356). The plan is never the source of truth for the link afterwards; a stale or withdrawn plan leaves its tasks governed. `rule_version` records the rule version current when the link was made, and the link resolves to the rule's newest version. A link may be pinned when it is made (`--pin`); a pinned link resolves to that version and reports the versioned page `/projects/<proj>/rule/<n>/<ver>`. Governing the same rule again without the pin unpins it. After minting, only an architect changes the links, by hand, and every change is an event on the task (`task.governed`, `task.ungoverned`). A link's `source` is `plan`, `manual` or `gate`: the plan that minted the task, an architect's hand, or the design authority gate reading a `Spec:` trailer on a planless task's pull request (WL-REQ-7). The gate writes only when no plan link exists and never removes a link. A task created without a plan may name its rules at creation and may acquire them later. A refactor (`lode rule supersede`) never moves a task's link: a task governed by a rule the refactor withdraws keeps that link, and it reads the live rules the withdrawn rule resolves to by following `supersedes` edges from the old rule to the rules that replace it, transitively. Each task the refactor touches this way gets one `task.governance_superseded` event naming the old rule and its successors; the link rows themselves are untouched. Those events live in the event log only; task timelines show state transitions and leave governance changes to the task detail and `lode event tail`. Re-accepting a plan whose `covers` widened governs only the tasks that re-accept publishes; earlier tasks keep their links until an architect adds to them. A rule ref carries its project key, so a task may be governed by another project's rule. When a plan closes, by `lode doc withdraw` or by its last task closing, every task minted from it that carries no governing link is linked to the rules the plan's `covers` edges point at before the status moves, so a closed plan's tasks each carry at least one link.
